A. Primary Textbook (Mandatory)
1. Digital Image Processing (4th Edition) – Gonzalez & Woods (Pearson)
Authors
• Rafael C. Gonzalez 
• Richard E. Woods 
This should be the primary textbook for the course.
Relevant chapters:
Module Chapters
Introduction Ch. 1
Image Fundamentals Ch. 2
Enhancement Ch. 3
Frequency Domain Ch. 4
Restoration Ch. 5
Wavelets Ch. 6
Color Processing Ch. 7
Compression Ch. 8 (selected)
Morphology Ch. 9
Segmentation Ch. 10
Feature Extraction & Recognition Ch. 11–12
The 4th edition also includes expanded material on deep learning, SIFT, graph cuts, 
superpixels, active contours, and 120 MATLAB projects, making it suitable for a modern 
DIP course. 
B. MATLAB Companion (Highly Recommended)
2. Digital Image Processing Using MATLAB (3rd Edition)
Authors
• Gonzalez 
• Woods 
• Steven Eddins (MathWorks) 
This book complements the primary text by providing:
• MATLAB implementations 
• Image Processing Toolbox usage 
• Deep Learning Toolbox examples 
• More than 130 programming projects 
• Downloadable support packages and image datasets 
C. Companion Computer Vision Text
3. Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications (Richard Szeliski)
Recommended chapters:
• Feature Detection 
• Stereo Vision

• Motion 
• Recognition 
• Segmentation 
• Deep Learning 
This is one of the best free references for bridging classical DIP with modern Computer 
Vision. It is widely recommended alongside Gonzalez & Woods.

Suggested Reference List for the Syllabus (Download the coloured references)
1. R. C. Gonzalez and R. E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, 4th Edition, Pearson. 
(Primary Text) 
2. R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, and S. L. Eddins, Digital Image Processing Using 
MATLAB, 3rd Edition. 
3. Richard Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications (Free online). 
4. Wilhelm Burger and Mark Burge, Digital Image Processing: An Algorithmic 
Introduction using Java. 
5. Anil K. Jain, Fundamentals of Digital Image Processing. 
6. OpenCV Documentation. 
7. MATLAB Image Processing Toolbox Documentation. 
8. scikit-image Documentation. 
9. PyTorch Tutorials. 
10. Ultralytics YOLO Documentation. 
This combination gives students a complete learning path:
• Gonzalez & Woods for theory and mathematics, 
• Digital Image Processing Using MATLAB for laboratory implementation, 
• Szeliski for modern computer vision concepts, 
• PyTorch/YOLO/Hugging Face for the final deep learning and transformer modules.
